hints: Focus on the two key regions in IR, the broad O-H stretch around 2500 to 3500 and the sharp C=O stretch around 1700.
Notice spectrum 1 has a very sharp strong peak near 1700 but no broad O-H hump, so it must contain C=O alone.
Compare spectra 2 and 3, one has both a very broad low O-H plus C=O, the other has a cleaner alcohol O-H with no C=O, match these to acid and alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Recall the fingerprint functional groups**

Think like a detective. Three compounds differ by one key group each. Propanone is a ketone, propanoic acid is a carboxylic acid, propan-2-ol is an alcohol.

Key IR rules:
$$\text{C=O stretch: sharp strong peak at } 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{O-H (alcohol): broad peak at } 3200-3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
$$\text{O-H (acid): very broad hump at } 2500-3300 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

**Analyse spectrum 1**

Look at spectrum 1. There is a tall sharp dip near $1450$ to $1700 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ for C=O, plus C-H peaks near $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

There is no broad O-H hump above $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$. That means C=O with no O-H, so this is the ketone, propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$.

**Analyse spectrum 2**

Now look at spectrum 2. It also has a strong C=O peak near $1700 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, but it also has a huge very broad absorption from about $2500$ to $3300 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

That extra broad low hump is classic for hydrogen bonded O-H in a carboxylic acid. So this is propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$.

**Analyse spectrum 3 and conclude**

Finally look at spectrum 3. It has a broad rounded O-H peak centred near $3350 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, but no sharp C=O peak near $1700 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

O-H with no C=O means an alcohol. So this is propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Putting it together gives propanone, propanoic acid, propan-2-ol.

options.A: Incorrect. Spectrum 1 cannot be propanoic acid because it lacks the very broad acid O-H hump from 2500 to 3300 cm-1. It shows only C=O, which fits a ketone.
options.B: Correct. Spectrum 1 is propanone with sharp C=O and no O-H, spectrum 2 is propanoic acid with both C=O and very broad acid O-H, spectrum 3 is propan-2-ol with broad alcohol O-H and no C=O.
options.C: Incorrect. Spectrum 2 is not propan-2-ol because it clearly shows a strong C=O peak near 1700 cm-1, which an alcohol does not have. Spectrum 3 is not the acid because it has no C=O peak.
options.D: Incorrect. Spectrum 1 is not propan-2-ol because it has a strong C=O peak and no broad alcohol O-H. Spectrum 3 is not propanone because it has a broad O-H but no C=O peak.
